entries.681a8f729a6dd6da: A business that invests entrusted savings in securities such as government bonds and foreign bonds. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, ordinary revenue from external customers was ¥2,281,877 million (¥2,215,355 million in the previous fiscal year), the largest of the four categories. At the end of March 2026, securities totaled ¥145.3 trillion, comprising ¥41.4 trillion in government bonds and ¥88.2 trillion in other securities. Taking advantage of rising domestic interest rates, it continues to shift investment from due-from-banks deposits and others into Japanese government bonds, and is advancing the sophistication and diversification of its investments through international diversified investment and investment in alternative assets (such as private equity funds). For the non-consolidated fiscal year ended March 2026, interest on government bonds was ¥368,351 million (¥257,945 million in the previous fiscal year), and interest on foreign securities was ¥1,403,088 million (¥1,242,068 million in the previous fiscal year).

entries.b7a3fc41eb240078: This business provides services and products through its head office and branches, other offices (directly operated stores), the post office network of Japan Post Co., Ltd., and various digital channels, and receives fees for them. In its description of the business, it calls this the "fee business" and lists remittance services, sales of asset management products such as government bonds and investment trusts, credit card services, housing loan brokerage services, and ATM partnership services in cooperation with other financial institutions. Ordinary income from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥196,841 million (¥184,839 million in the previous year), the third largest of the four categories.

entries.d93a462220f1ba35: This business provides loans through syndicated loan operations and account overdraft services, among others. Because most deposits are invested in securities, the scale of lending is small, and ordinary income from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥23,864 million (¥12,140 million in the previous year), the smallest of the four categories. This amount is the same as the interest on loans shown in the non-consolidated funds management table (¥23,864 million). Loans as of the end of March 2026 were ¥4.3721 trillion, an increase of ¥1.2415 trillion from the end of the previous fiscal year. Of domestic loans (non-consolidated), loans to national and local governments amounted to ¥3,408,950 million (composition ratio: 78.16%). It is strengthening fund supply to local governments and, in cooperation with regional financial institutions, is also investing in regional revitalization funds. Credit guarantee and administrative services for the account overdraft service are carried out by Yucho Loan Center Co., Ltd., a 100%-owned subsidiary.
entries.f3c0ffbb178df4ac: A bank that, under the Banking Act, accepts savings deposits up to the deposit ceiling and invests those savings mainly in securities. Using the post office network of Japan Post Co., Ltd. as its main channel, it provides financial services to customers on a scale of 120 million people. At the end of March 2026, savings totaled ¥186.1 trillion, of which individual savings accounted for more than 90%. Securities totaled ¥145.3 trillion, of which government bonds were ¥41.4 trillion, and “other securities,” including foreign bonds and investment trusts whose main investment target is foreign bonds, were ¥88.2 trillion. The deposit ceiling for savings is ¥13 million each for ordinary savings and fixed-term savings, and ¥5.5 million combined for employee savings (from April 1, 2019). In addition to 235 head offices, branches and other business offices nationwide, it entrusts banking agency services and others to Japan Post Co., Ltd., and has agencies at 19,701 post offices and 3,370 simplified post offices (as of March 31, 2026). The group consists of the bank, 18 [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]], one equity-method affiliate and others, and forms a single [[term:segment|segment]] for banking. Management is pursued through three business strategies: “Retail Business,” “Market Business” and “Σ Business.” For the fiscal year ended March 2026, consolidated ordinary revenue was ¥2,852,206 million (¥2,522,052 million in the previous fiscal year), and the number of employees was 10,771.
